messages:
sam: FYI scheduling a quiet-hour window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC to run egress-buffer priming + KV prefix seeding in us-east1. Low traffic, want to pre-warm caches before expected morning surge.

nina: sounds good — what's the expected capacity hit? any tenant throttles?

sam: estimate ~6% extra GPU cycles for 20m during warmup. we'll throttle by tenant priority and bypass low-priority spot pools. no tenant eviction planned.

rachel: cost question — will this incur measurable billable GPU time? can we tag the job for cost center? :money_with_wings:

sam: yes will be billable. tagging plan: env=maintenance, cc=infra-preseed. run will use reserved pool credits where possible to lower unit cost.

diego: prepping the seed job now. command i'll run: ```./scripts/kv_seed --region us-east1 --pool=reserved-gradient --prefixes=2000 --concurrency=8 --dry-run=false```

opsbot: [scheduler] Maintenance window created: id=mw-70807-egress-seed, start=7080708090, end=7080711690, owner=sam

nina: if prefix seeding pushes egressthroughput, do we have an egress fallback route? i.e. route traffic to eu fallback for heavy tails?

sam: yes — routing policy preconfigured: latency-sensitive -> fallback to us-west1, batch/low-priority -> queue & backpressure. automatic graceful failover if egress qlen > 85%.

rachel: can we add a short alert to #incidents if average token latency rises > 250ms for 5m? want to catch regressions early.

sam: good call. adding alert: infra.egress.latency.avg > 250ms for 5m -> notify @oncall + #incidents. also dashboard spike panel: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/egress/priming-run

diego: sharing a small log sample after a dry-run earlier: ```[kv_seed] prefix=100..1500 seeded=1400 errors=0 throughput=1.2k/s p95_latency=18ms```

nina: runbook question — if we hit 10% error rate during seeding, do we abort and rollback cache entries?

sam: yes. abort thresholds: errors >= 5% for 2 consecutive minutes => stop job, roll back ephemeral prefixes, and open incident. fallback: enable on-demand model fanout to read-through (slower but safe).

rachel: confirm no customer-facing downtime expected?

sam: correct. all routing is graceful and we keep SLAs. we'll keep customers informed only if we cross thresholds. internal comms only unless major impact.

diego: kicking off actual run at +5m per prep checklist. i'll post completion log when done.

opsbot: [runbook] Checklist link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/egress-priming — step 3 = monitor kv_seed job, step 6 = validate model latency p50/p95.

nina: thanks. i'll watch the dashboards and help triage if anything weird pops up. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all — i'll post a short summary after window closes with cost delta and any anomalies.
